title: Reason Code 8 — the user account does not exist
plain_english: NPS looked up the account name the device sent and found nothing. The password never got checked — the identity itself didn't resolve. The interesting question is what name the device actually transmitted, and that's printed right in this event.

causes.cause: The username is typed on the device in a format NPS can't resolve — bare name vs DOMAIN\\user vs user@domain (UPN), or with a stray space.
causes.next_check: Compare the 'Account Name' in this event with the real sAMAccountName/UPN in AD; re-enter it on the device in the working format.

causes.cause: The device is doing machine authentication ('host/NAME' identity) but the computer account doesn't exist in the domain — common for BYOD or freshly re-imaged machines.
causes.next_check: If the User Name starts with 'host/', check whether that computer object exists in AD and is not disabled.

causes.cause: The account lives in a different domain/forest and the trust path or the NPS server's search scope doesn't reach it.
causes.next_check: Verify the domain prefix in the event and confirm the trust between that domain and the NPS server's domain.
